item.text: {"results":[{"pair_id":"J03575","case1_error":"Treats 15 training days per stage as 15 weeks, omitting division by five training days per week.","case2_error":"Uses daily calorie deficit instead of calories required per pound to calculate the deficit needed for ten pounds.","reason":"Case 1 omits a time-unit conversion; case 2 substitutes the wrong rate when calculating the required total deficit.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J03576","case1_error":"Uses two weeks of doubled vegetable consumption as the weekly amount, then adds one week's kale.","case2_error":"Equates occupied chairs with attendees, omitting the two people seated in each occupied chair.","reason":"Case 1 aggregates consumption over the wrong time interval; case 2 fails to convert occupied chairs into people.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J03577","case1_error":"Adds increases for all three inches grown to the baseline probability, although the baseline applies at 66 inches.","case2_error":"No mathematical error: one quarter correctly expresses the probability of selecting a blue candy.","reason":"Case 1 uses the wrong height baseline. Case 2 is correct; its fraction equals the reference's 25%.","judgment":"uncertain"},{"pair_id":"J03578","case1_error":"Reports brownies given to Carl and Simon as brownies remaining, instead of subtracting those gifts from ten.","case2_error":"Subtracts mint plants from the basil-only count and omits parsley when determining the final total.","reason":"Case 1 answers with the quantity given away; case 2 uses a category subtotal as the starting total for subtraction.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J03579","case1_error":"Calculates primer cost at full price, ignoring the specified 20% discount.","case2_error":"Gives an unsupported final ratio of 11/2 after correctly stating formulas that yield 10.","reason":"Case 1 omits a required discount in its calculation; case 2 supplies an incorrect final number without showing its evaluation.","judgment":"different"}]}
